newsitem.title: USA: Dollar's continued rise may compel action - NYT.
newsitem.headline: Dollar's continued rise may compel action - NYT.

text.p: U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin and his G7 allies want to rein in the dollar, but a sentence they included in their statement backing this goal may have unintentionally given traders reason to push the dollar even higher, the New York Times said Thursday.
The paper said the 11-word sentence is, "We reaffirmed our views that exchange rates should reflect economic fundamentals."

"The one thing that we took away from that statement was that the central banks are serious and that they think that fundamentals should drive the dollar," Audrey McNiff, the vice president in foreign exchange sales at Goldman Sachs & Co, told the paper.

The report said recent gains in unemployment in Germany and Switzerland and poor reports from both countries' business communities were being taken as a sign that Europe's economic situation is worsening.
Because economic fundamentals may favor the dollar, officials could be forced sooner than they might like to take action, the report said.

Such action could begin with verbal jawboning from Rubin and other finance ministers, followed with intervention by the U.S. and other countries that would sell dollars to lower the value, the paper said.
But analysts believe such actions are unlikely to have more than a temporary effect, the paper said.
"The intriguing question is when the G-7 ministers think their credibility is at stake and they have to do something," John Lipsky, the chief economist at Chase Manhattan Bank, told the paper.
